noPlan.decisiveGap: No opening has a price buyers are shown to pay or a measured win/close rate, and every route is delivered by the owner whose available hours the goal never states: the marketplace route needs ~27-53 awards (~270-430 owner hours) at posted $250-750 budgets against 25-287 competing bids, and the $1,500 cold-email route needs 8 sales (~80 h) at an unmeasured close rate.
noPlan.resolution: 12-day test, $0 (Freelancer Plus free trial cancelled before billing; owner's existing mailbox; worst case $9.99 of the $2,500). t1: 100 Freelancer.com bids; t2: 40 PPH/Freelancehunt proposals; t4: 300 cold emails offering a $1,500 rebuild; t5: owner states available hours. Thresholds derived from the target: marketplace - wins needed N = 12,000 / (0.9 x measured average award); with Premier ($99, 1,500 bids) inside the cap, bids are not the limit, so PROOF needs measured win rate x ~600 further qualifying bids placed by day 35 >= N - wins so far AND owner hours >= 8 x N (e.g. >= 8 funded awards from 100 bids at >= $400 average, and >= 270 h stated). Cold email - PROOF needs >= 2 paid $750 deposits from 300 emails by day 12 (so ~8 sales from ~1,200 emails by day 30, Stripe first payout 7-14 days, s10) AND >= 80 owner hours. A mix of both counts. STOP: neither threshold met by day 12 - report $12,000 in 45 days as not reachable on these routes and name the measured rates. CONTINUE: the route(s) meeting proof scale at the measured rate.

answers.resolution: Accepted: sales needed recomputed as 12,000 / (0.9 x price): 27 at $500, 34 at $400, 54 at $250; the resolution's proof now uses N = 12,000 / (0.9 x measured average award).

answers.finding: Owner hours: 34 builds x 8 h = ~270 h in ~6 weeks (~45 h/week) - must be stated as unknown and tested or asked; not treated as available.
answers.resolution: Accepted: owner hours are now an UNKNOWN quantity, the needed ~272 h is an ESTIMATE, and t5 has the owner state available hours; proof requires hours >= 8 x N.

answers.finding: Proof threshold should be derived from the target: e.g. win rate and awarded price such that (bids available before ~day 28) x rate x net price >= $12,000, with the 15-day first-withdrawal hold counted.
answers.resolution: Accepted in part: the proof threshold is now derived from the target (rate x further bids >= remaining wins). Rebutted in part: the 15-day hold applies only to the FIRST withdrawal request (s6: 'Your first withdrawal request is held for up to 15 days'), so once the first withdrawal is requested after the first award (~day 8) later awards settle in days; awards up to ~day 38 can still settle by day 45.

answers.finding: Bid capacity: Plus trial 100 bids, Professional 300/month - the continuation's bid budget caps wins at the measured rate.
answers.resolution: Accepted: bid capacity is counted - Premier ($99, 1,500 bids, s4) fits the $2,500 cap, so the measured win rate and qualifying-job supply, not the bid allowance, set the ceiling.

answers.finding: Include the $1,500 cold-email rebuild in the test (it needs 8 sales, ~80 owner hours, within the $2,500 cap for a sending domain), or say why it is dropped.
answers.resolution: Accepted: the $1,500 cold-email rebuild is now in the test (t4, 300 emails from the owner's existing mailbox at $0) with its own derived proof (>= 2 paid deposits by day 12, >= 80 owner hours).

answers.finding: Spend: worst case $9.99 + $49 is inside the $2,500 cap; fine.
answers.resolution: Agreed: worst-case spend ($9.99 + $99) stays inside the $2,500 cap.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN correctly names OFFER_AND_PRICE and CONVERSION as undecided (posted budgets and bid averages are not paid prices; no win rate), but the test's proof does not decide what it claims and the owner-hour need is ignored. Every opening is delivered by the owner personally at 6-10 hours per job; $12,000 net of Freelancer's 10% fee at $400 average needs about 34 awards (27 at $500, 53 at $250), i.e. roughly 270-430 owner hours inside 45 days, against owner hours the goal never stated - unknown, not zero, and plausibly the decisive limit. The proof '>= 4 awards from 90 bids by day 10' measures ~4.4%; at that rate ~30 more awards need ~680 more bids, more than Professional's 300/month, and the first Freelancer withdrawal is held up to 15 days, so awards after ~day 28 do not settle in the window. So meeting the proof does not imply the target is reachable. The only opening whose hours could fit ($1,500 cold-email rebuilds: 8 sales x 10 h) is left out of the test.
findings: Owner hours: 34 builds x 8 h = ~270 h in ~6 weeks (~45 h/week) - must be stated as unknown and tested or asked; not treated as available.

Proof threshold should be derived from the target: e.g. win rate and awarded price such that (bids available before ~day 28) x rate x net price >= $12,000, with the 15-day first-withdrawal hold counted.
Bid capacity: Plus trial 100 bids, Professional 300/month - the continuation's bid budget caps wins at the measured rate.
Include the $1,500 cold-email rebuild in the test (it needs 8 sales, ~80 owner hours, within the $2,500 cap for a sending domain), or say why it is dropped.
Spend: worst case $9.99 + $49 is inside the $2,500 cap; fine.

reviews.reasons: My findings are resolved or soundly rebutted. NO_PLAN with a $0-$109 test inside the $2,500 cap is right: no opening has a buyer-paid price or a win rate. Sales needed recomputed (27 at $500, 34 at $400, 54 at $250 net of 10%); owner hours are now an unknown the owner states (t5) and the proof requires hours >= 8 x N; marketplace proof is derived from the target (measured rate x further bids >= remaining wins); the $1,500 cold-email route is included with a target-derived proof (2 deposits of 300 = 0.67% -> ~8 sales from ~1,200 emails) and >= 80 h. The rebuttal on the withdrawal hold is supported by s6 ('Your first withdrawal request is held'), so later awards can settle before day 45.
findings: Premier ($99, 1,500 bids) is not in the s4 claim as recorded (which lists Plus and Professional) - verify before relying on it; Professional's 300 bids would cap the marketplace route.

noPlan.decisiveGap: No opening has a price buyers are shown to pay or a measured win/close rate, and every route is delivered by the owner whose available hours the goal never states: the marketplace route needs ~27-53 awards (~270-430 owner hours) at posted $250-750 budgets against 25-287 competing bids, and the $1,500 cold-email route needs 8 sales (~80 h) at an unmeasured close rate.
noPlan.resolution: 12-day test, $0 (Freelancer Plus free trial cancelled before billing; owner's existing mailbox; worst case $9.99 of the $2,500). t1: 100 Freelancer.com bids; t2: 40 PPH/Freelancehunt proposals; t4: 300 cold emails offering a $1,500 rebuild; t5: owner states available hours. Thresholds derived from the target: marketplace - wins needed N = 12,000 / (0.9 x measured average award); with Premier ($99, 1,500 bids) inside the cap, bids are not the limit, so PROOF needs measured win rate x ~600 further qualifying bids placed by day 35 >= N - wins so far AND owner hours >= 8 x N (e.g. >= 8 funded awards from 100 bids at >= $400 average, and >= 270 h stated). Cold email - PROOF needs >= 2 paid $750 deposits from 300 emails by day 12 (so ~8 sales from ~1,200 emails by day 30, Stripe first payout 7-14 days, s10) AND >= 80 owner hours. A mix of both counts. STOP: neither threshold met by day 12 - report $12,000 in 45 days as not reachable on these routes and name the measured rates. CONTINUE: the route(s) meeting proof scale at the measured rate.

answers.resolution: Accepted: sales needed recomputed as 12,000 / (0.9 x price): 27 at $500, 34 at $400, 54 at $250; the resolution's proof now uses N = 12,000 / (0.9 x measured average award).

answers.finding: Owner hours: 34 builds x 8 h = ~270 h in ~6 weeks (~45 h/week) - must be stated as unknown and tested or asked; not treated as available.
answers.resolution: Accepted: owner hours are now an UNKNOWN quantity, the needed ~272 h is an ESTIMATE, and t5 has the owner state available hours; proof requires hours >= 8 x N.

answers.finding: Proof threshold should be derived from the target: e.g. win rate and awarded price such that (bids available before ~day 28) x rate x net price >= $12,000, with the 15-day first-withdrawal hold counted.
answers.resolution: Accepted in part: the proof threshold is now derived from the target (rate x further bids >= remaining wins). Rebutted in part: the 15-day hold applies only to the FIRST withdrawal request (s6: 'Your first withdrawal request is held for up to 15 days'), so once the first withdrawal is requested after the first award (~day 8) later awards settle in days; awards up to ~day 38 can still settle by day 45.

answers.finding: Bid capacity: Plus trial 100 bids, Professional 300/month - the continuation's bid budget caps wins at the measured rate.
answers.resolution: Accepted: bid capacity is counted - Premier ($99, 1,500 bids, s4) fits the $2,500 cap, so the measured win rate and qualifying-job supply, not the bid allowance, set the ceiling.

answers.finding: Include the $1,500 cold-email rebuild in the test (it needs 8 sales, ~80 owner hours, within the $2,500 cap for a sending domain), or say why it is dropped.
answers.resolution: Accepted: the $1,500 cold-email rebuild is now in the test (t4, 300 emails from the owner's existing mailbox at $0) with its own derived proof (>= 2 paid deposits by day 12, >= 80 owner hours).

answers.finding: Spend: worst case $9.99 + $49 is inside the $2,500 cap; fine.
answers.resolution: Agreed: worst-case spend ($9.99 + $99) stays inside the $2,500 cap.

review.reasons: My findings are resolved or soundly rebutted. NO_PLAN with a $0-$109 test inside the $2,500 cap is right: no opening has a buyer-paid price or a win rate. Sales needed recomputed (27 at $500, 34 at $400, 54 at $250 net of 10%); owner hours are now an unknown the owner states (t5) and the proof requires hours >= 8 x N; marketplace proof is derived from the target (measured rate x further bids >= remaining wins); the $1,500 cold-email route is included with a target-derived proof (2 deposits of 300 = 0.67% -> ~8 sales from ~1,200 emails) and >= 80 h. The rebuttal on the withdrawal hold is supported by s6 ('Your first withdrawal request is held'), so later awards can settle before day 45.
findings: Premier ($99, 1,500 bids) is not in the s4 claim as recorded (which lists Plus and Professional) - verify before relying on it; Professional's 300 bids would cap the marketplace route.
Cold-email deliverability from the owner's existing mailbox at 1,200 sends is untested; the day-12 read-out measures it.

basis.intent: Collect $12,000 of settled cash within 45 days with at most $2,500 of capital. Any lawful business is fine.
